resources.string: Primary screen-on filtering for selected headset key events delivered by Android Accessibility. It does not inspect screen contents or typed text.
Silence headset controls. Keep the phone buttons yours.
Accessibility filters screen-on. Shizuku exclusively guards the selected headset’s raw button input before Android receives media, volume, or call-control presses, including screen off.
Accessibility is filtering screen-on. Shizuku’s media listener covers ordinary screen-off media routing, but call-safe screen-off protection requires selecting the headset input.
Accessibility is filtering headset buttons now. The exclusive selected-headset guard is unavailable or still reconnecting through Shizuku.
Accessibility is filtering screen-on and Shizuku’s media listener is active, but screen-off call-control safety still requires the selected-headset raw guard.
Accessibility is filtering headset buttons now. Screen-off Shizuku protection is off.
Shizuku is exclusively guarding the selected headset’s raw button input, including call-control and volume presses. Enable Accessibility for the primary screen-on path.
Shizuku’s media listener is active, but screen-off call-control safety is not guaranteed until the headset input is selected and exclusively guarded.
Shizuku is connected, but the requested selected-headset safety route is not active yet. Automatic recovery is armed.
Connecting the privileged guard and finding the headset input. Nothing is shown as protected until both are ready.
Accessibility filtering and Shizuku screen-off protection are off.
Screen-off protection needs Shizuku. Screen-on Accessibility filtering can still work independently.
Start Shizuku to continue protection setup. Your protection switch will stay off until setup is complete.
Grant Button Silencer access to restore screen-off protection. Accessibility can keep filtering screen-on.
Grant Shizuku access to continue. Protection will turn on only after the headset route is ready.
The screen-off Shizuku engine is attaching. The main protection switch stays usable while it connects.
Select your USB DAC / IEM for the strongest call-safe protection. Matching remote-control input nodes are guarded together.
Only the chosen external headset’s matching remote-control input nodes are exclusively guarded. The phone’s built-in side-button nodes are never grabbed.
Required for call-safe raw-input protection when the screen is off. Accessibility remains the primary screen-on filter.
Screen-off protection is enabled. Scan and select the headset to add the exclusive call-safe raw-input guard.
Select the headset input device first.
The selected-headset safety guard stays on while Shizuku screen-off protection is enabled. Turn off screen-off media protection first if you want to disable it.
No external headset-control input was found. Connect the headset, keep Shizuku running, and scan again.
Only devices that look like the phone’s own buttons were found, so none were offered.

The selected-headset route is the strongest path: Shizuku exclusively grabs its remote-control input node(s) before Android receives media, volume, or call-control events. The media listener remains a broader screen-off media route, but is not treated as a call-safety guarantee. Recovery is event-driven with bounded retries; there is no wake lock or polling loop.

These rules apply only while Android’s Accessibility service is enabled and Button Silencer filtering is active. Call-capable headset hook / play-pause / call / end-call keys are always blocked while protection is on.
Block volume keys from every device
Caution: the last option can also disable the phone’s own volume buttons while Accessibility receives them.
Accessibility filtering is off in Android. Enable the service for the primary screen-on blocking path.
Active now. Accessibility is the primary screen-on button filter.
Android service is available, but Button Silencer filtering is paused.
Accessibility settings are unavailable on this device.
Headset selected. Protection is turning on.
Off by default for minimum overhead. When enabled, recognized events are kept only in memory for this app session and are never sent anywhere.
No recognized Accessibility events in this session.
A compact Android utility for suppressing unwanted headset controls while keeping the phone’s physical buttons usable.
No network permission, analytics, ads, account, USB interface claim, continuous polling loop, or persistent event history.
Accessibility handles screen-on filtering. For call-safe screen-off blocking, keep Shizuku running and select the headset input so its raw control nodes can be exclusively guarded.
